idiom_name: interface UserDAO + factory function over a Record<Store, (cfg) => UserDAO> registry
implementation_notes: TypeScript keeps the DAO contract as an interface and reduces the factory to a function over a Record keyed by a union of store names, which makes the store set exhaustive and the lookup compile-checked; implementations are modules or classes satisfying the interface. The compiler replaces the runtime checks the catalog form wrote by hand, so no class hierarchy is warranted; keep the registry at the composition root and prefer a discriminated union of configuration over untyped config objects. Interfaces are erased at runtime, which matters as soon as a DI framework needs a runtime token.
pitfalls: Interfaces are erased at runtime and cannot be DI tokens (NestJS needs a class, string or Symbol token), so a registry keyed by interface type fails where a token is required.

A Record typed by the store union is exhaustive for literals, but a store name arriving from configuration is a plain string and must be validated (type guard or schema parse) before it is treated as Store.
Async DAO construction (dynamic import or lazy clients) changes the factory's return type to Promise<UserDAO>; mixing synchronous and asynchronous registries complicates lifecycle and error handling.

variants.name: NestJS useFactory provider
variants.idiom_name: custom provider { provide: USER_DAO, useFactory, inject }
variants.implementation_notes: In a NestJS application the container is the factory: register the DAO under a string or Symbol token with a useFactory provider whose dependencies are declared in inject, so the store key can come from a configuration provider and the matching implementation is constructed once for the right scope. Interfaces cannot be tokens because types are erased, so the token is the DI identity while the interface stays the compile-time shape. This replaces hand-written factories wherever Nest is already the composition root; a plain registry remains simpler in non-framework code.
pitfalls: Interfaces cannot be provider tokens; registering provide: UserDAO fails at runtime, so use a Symbol or string token and @Inject(USER_DAO).
useFactory providers are instantiated per scope: a DAO built as a singleton while injecting a request-scoped client captures the first request's connection - align scopes or use durable providers.
Decorator metadata needs experimentalDecorators and emitDecoratorMetadata; changing TypeScript decorator mode alters how Nest resolves constructor types.
